instruction_changes.deviation: The frontend owner retained acceptance obligations but did not specify a minimal selected-version handoff, transfer readback, bounded frontend batches and dependency-scoped evidence reuse together. A broad source-invalidation workflow could restart unrelated verification during small comparisons.
instruction_changes.evidence: The user explicitly approved the proposed lightweight additions and authorized publication from this side conversation. Preserve labs for unresolved visual choices; leave the complete private pipeline unadopted.
instruction_changes.why_instruction: Extend the existing frontend working sequence for explicit reusable user preferences. Existing selected-versus-finished and retained-finding requirements remain authoritative; no new tool, schema, workflow owner or historical project mapping is installed.
instruction_changes.alternative: No change retains missing practical triggers. Full pipeline adoption imposes broad collection/review after small edits without demonstrated outcome or cost benefit. Existing transfer helpers remain conditional; no transfer tool is needed for wholly local comparisons.

source_boundaries: Iterative batches choose outcome, baseline and project effort ceiling; an exact one-off repair needs no budget document.
Chosen visual settings and exact receiving files are recorded; visual selection leaves functional defects open.
Changed rendering dependencies require affected checks and neighbors; unchanged independent evidence can be reused with scoped justification.
Reuse cannot clear missing evidence or manufacture whole-product acceptance.
Transfer helpers apply only when environments differ; existing lab guidance, approvals and regression commitments remain unchanged.
checks.ownership_purpose: Existing frontend objective, added value and retirement test retained.

limits: Source decision-boundary checks and publication/readback only; no fresh model comparison, cost measurement or behavioral parity claim.
No private V15 source or project-specific historical findings are published.
